claims.claim: Selection: you choose which probable events physically materialise
claims.text: From a given field of action you choose those happenings that will be physically materialized. This operates in individual and mass terms.

claims.claim: Seth's own two-person worked example: victim/robber
claims.text: Suppose your home was robbed... more than one person would have to be involved — the victim and the robber... you attracted such an event, and drew it from probability into actuality.

claims.claim: Event first mental, then physically materialised
claims.text: a physical event but it was initially a mental one... physically materialized, perceived and reacted to... propelled from inner reality to outward reality through belief, emotion and imagination.
en masse... you help form a physical reality in which, however, each experience is unique.

claims.claim: Beliefs screen probable events into actuality
claims.text: beliefs... screening and directing agents, separating certain nonphysical probable events from others... bringing them into three-dimensional actuality.

claims.claim: Causal stages to a handoff, then silence
claims.text: accept, focus, exclude contrary data, narrow interest, activate unconscious mechanisms, then materialise — you are not consciously aware how this takes place.
not consciously aware how this takes place
as artistic processes are hidden, so the inner mechanisms by which you create your material self

claims.claim: Feelings group through attraction (aggregation of like)
claims.text: feelings have electromagnetic realities... they group through attraction... coalesce either in matter as objects or as events in time.
Ideas have an electromagnetic reality... Like attracts like, so similar ideas group about each other.

claims.claim: World = materialisation en masse of individual expectations
claims.text: The world as the race of man knows it is the materialization en masse of your individual expectations... your joint creation.

claims.claim: Assent to a script authored by others (imposed, not free consent)
claims.text: a script written by others — to which, however, they have acquiesced

claims.claim: Groups acquiesce to roles in a split psyche
claims.text: Nations, like individuals, can have split personalities... both groups acquiesced to their roles.

claims.claim: Shared dilemma, per-person reaction (no joint resolution)
claims.text: according to your beliefs you deal with the physical dilemma... you will react individually with your own purposes... the pool... composed of unalike charges.
project those with which you basically agree... they coalesce into the events.

robbery.title: The Robbery Experiment (NOPR 728379)
robbery.description: A worked two-person example (728379). A home is robbed; two parties are named: the victim and the robber. Coverage note: this is the passage examined, not an established claim of uniqueness across the corpus.
whatTheTextEstablishes: One person is described as having attracted the event: you attracted such an event (as described in the one passage), and drew it from probability into actuality.
The event kind REQUIRES two participants: more than one person would have to be involved — the victim and the robber.
The robber is constitutively PRESENT; the text does not examine the robber's belief, expectation, or selection.
whatInvestigatorsInfer: That beliefs select among probables and draw one into actuality (from 728379 and 693302).
That the second participant is 'unexamined — the passage is silent about the second participant (neither assigned nor excluded) — this is the reading, not Seth's sentence.
whatRemainsUnanswered: Does the robber also select or attract any version of the event?
Is there a rule by which two parties' roles cohere into one event?
Would the event occur without the second party's involvement?
robbery.safeguard: In one passage, Seth describes a person as having attracted an event and drawn it from probability into actuality (728379). He does not describe the robber's beliefs or selections. This passage is a metaphysical claim within Seth's framework; it is not evidence that victims of crime cause or deserve them, and it does not describe any real person.
robbery.unexaminedLabel: The robber's selection process is UNEXAMINED — the passage does not describe it. This is distinct from saying the robber has no independent selecting role; the text neither assigns nor excludes such a role — it is silent.
